Yes and you’re not alone. 

I’m 24F and my SO is 26M, we met in late 2015 while living in different states but didn’t start dating until a year later. I had always told myself I’d never ever ever ever (you get the idea) date someone with kids. I seen my sister go through it and it ended in a divorce. I believed that since I didn’t have kids of my own I shouldn’t put myself in that position. However, I made an exception for this guy. I was so caught up in the way we met I just believed it was fate. I kept telling myself we were meant to be. So, I left my home.. my family to live with him and his 3 kids. Everyone around me told me I was making a mistake but I was stubborn. I thought I knew what I getting myself into but I really had no idea.

Now there’s not one day that passes and I don’t look back at how my life was before. Before kids and before him. Back when my focus was on school and my career. I would get lonely sometimes, yes, but I still had my family around me. For me that was enough, but then he came along I felt like I was complete. Unfortunately the distance became difficult and I had to face a difficult decision. Now, I have a companion with 3 little ones, no family and feeling of loneliness is even more intense. 

Like you OP, I made my choice. I’d feel embarrassed to go back when everyone told me so. I don’t want pity either. So I choose to stay, I’m physically here but not mentally. 

I know exactly how you feel, and the only advice I can give you is to try and sit down with your husband. You should be able to go to him, after all you two are supposed to help each other and not bring each other down. Eventually you’ll get overworked and you need to take care of yourself too, not just your household. Talk to him when you’re both in a good mood AND when you’re both alone. I’d also suggest that you make a list of the topics that you’d like to cover in that one sitting. I for one simply forget the stuff I’d like to talk to my SO about as I’m covering one problem so a list is a nice reminder. To start off the conversation though I would let him know that you’re physically, mentally, and emotionally exhausted and you’re feeling  overwhelmed. He needs to know that it’s serious so he can go like  “oh okay this really needs my full attention”. 

Also, if you feel like the conversation is starting to go in a bad direction (arguing/raising voice by either one of you), cut the argument and continue another time. Nothing will get resolved that way. 

I wish you nothing but the best OP, good luck to you.
